text: Weighing a star thousands of light-years away is hard, so every measurement comes with an uncertainty range. Two pulsars reach the critical regime. Demerest's measurement is 1.97 ± 0.04 solar masses. Its center is below 2. Fonseca's is 2.08 ± 0.07. The quoted 68.3% interval stays above 2. But at 95.4% credibility, the result does not clear too. At the quoted 68.3% level, the second measurement clears two solar masses. At the stricter 95.4% level, the closing record says it does not.
